newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: New Congo gets first police force for decades.
newsitem.headline: New Congo gets first police force for decades.

text.p: Laurent Kabila, president of the renamed Democratic Republic of Congo, has recreated the police, a force which ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko abolished decades ago, state radio reported on Saturday.
The resuscitated police force replaces both the anti-riot civil guard and the bloated gendarmerie that Mobutu used mostly to crack down on Zairean political dissent.
Initially the new force will comprise just two companies -- about 60 men.
"It's a rapid intervention force, in case of emergency or necessity," the radio said, adding that the policemen were already operating in the capital Kinshasa.
Mobutu, who grabbed power in 1965, dissolved the police force in the late 1960s and replaced it with the 30,000 strong gendarmerie.
A decade ago, he formed the civil guard which earned the hostility of the people by breaking up demonstrations, often with live fire used on crowds without warning.
State radio quoted new police chief Celestin Kifwa as saying his officers would also be seen in the interior of the vast central African country in the next few days.

Kabila, who seized power in May after a seven-month civil war, has pledged wide-ranging reforms in a country whose state insitutions -- courts, schools, hospitals and government -- withered away under Mobutu's rule.
